title: Tax Operations Note: Sales Tax Exemption Certificates on Small Business Electricity Supply Agreements
content:
A sales tax exemption on a Small Business Electricity Supply agreement is recorded only after Beacon Ridge tax operations has received and validated the business's exemption certificate; a representative's statement that the business is exempt does not change billing. The tax exemption date is the date the validated certificate was received, and the exemption applies from the billing cycles beginning on or after the tax exemption date. An exemption is recorded per agreement, so a business with several sites must provide a certificate covering each site. Sales tax billed before the exemption took effect is not refunded by Beacon Ridge; the business may seek a refund from the state tax authority.

## What establishes an exemption

| Evidence | Effect on billing |
|---|---|
| A certificate received and validated by tax operations | the agreement is marked exempt, with the tax exemption date |
| A representative's statement on a call that the business is exempt | none |
| A certificate covering one site only | the exemption is recorded on that site's agreement only |

## Which cycles are exempt (hypothetical dates)

A validated certificate is received on 12 May, which becomes the tax exemption date.

| Cycle | Begins | Sales tax |
|---|---|---|
| 3 April to 2 May | before 12 May | taxed |
| 3 May to 1 June | before 12 May | taxed |
| 2 June to 1 July | on or after 12 May | not taxed |

The two taxed cycles are not refunded by Beacon Ridge; the business may seek a refund of that tax from the state tax authority.

## Several sites

A business supplied at four sites that sends one certificate covering two of them has the exemption recorded on those two agreements; the other two agreements remain taxed until a certificate covering each of them is received and validated.
